title: Shadow Traffic: add LLM-as-judge scorer module + config model for shadow runs
creator: Jonas Weber
description:
Context
Shadow Traffic executes candidate model/config in the background against production-shaped requests and emits quality + perf signals. For release gating we need a repeatable comparative quality signal that works across heterogeneous tasks. This ticket adds an LLM-as-judge module to eval-harness plus a configuration model so shadow runs can:
- select a judge prompt/rubric,
- run either pairwise (primary vs shadow) or single-output rubric scoring,
- normalize to stable metrics (win-rate / score distributions),
- emit structured outputs compatible with shadow_eval.* schema.

Why now
Console + Rollouts want a first shipped “quality gate” signal that is more robust than raw similarity metrics. We will start with a minimal, constrained rubric and calibrated judge model choices, then iterate.

In scope
1) Eval-harness module: judge scorer (v1)
- Implement a scorer interface in eval-harness that can be called by the Shadow Runner pipeline (async) OR invoked downstream by telemetry/analytics if we decide to run scoring out-of-band.
- Support modes:
  a) Pairwise preference: judge chooses A/B (primary vs shadow), plus optional ‘tie/unclear’.
  b) Rubric scoring: judge assigns 1–5 (or 0–1) on rubric dimensions (e.g., instruction_following, format_adherence), returning JSON.
- Deterministic-ish prompting: fixed templates, strong JSON schema constraints, temperature=0 by default (where supported), enforce max tokens.
- Include response parsing + validation + fallback handling (invalid JSON, refusals, tool-call artifacts, etc.).
- Output normalization:
  - pairwise: win/loss/tie with confidence (if available) -> aggregated win_rate, tie_rate
  - rubric: per-dimension mean/p50/p90 + failure_rate (invalid/refusal)

2) Configuration model for shadow runs
- Define a config spec (JSON/YAML) that can be attached to a shadow target (or route policy) via control-plane and passed through to scoring.
- Fields include:
  - judge_model (catalog key, region constraints)
  - mode: pairwise|rubric
  - rubric_template_id (e.g., “shadow_v1_general”, “shadow_v1_json_schema”)
  - dimensions (allowlist) and weights (optional)
  - sampling controls for scoring (score only N% of shadowed requests if needed)
  - max_judge_tokens, timeout_ms, retries
  - redaction behavior: whether judge sees redacted input only vs redacted+truncated output

3) Telemetry output contract (producer-side)
- Emit a single per-(primary_request_id, shadow_request_id, scorer_id) result envelope in a structured form that telemetry can persist.
- Keep dimensions aligned with Observability standards + cardinality guardrails (ENG-2435). No free-form tags.

Out of scope (v1)
- Task-specific judge prompts authored per customer (we will ship only Redwood-provided templates in beta)
- Training / fine-tuning judge models
- Full “ground truth correctness” evaluation (judge is for comparative regression detection)
- Storing full prompts/outputs in eval-harness (storage/retention is handled by the shadow telemetry pipeline with redaction controls)

Proposed config model (draft)
Example (conceptual; final wire format to be confirmed with Platform/Policy team):

judge_scorer:
  scorer_id: shadow_judge_v1
  mode: pairwise
  judge_model: rw-judge-claude-3-5-sonnet  # placeholder catalog key
  template_id: shadow_v1_general_pairwise
  max_judge_tokens: 384
  timeout_ms: 2500
  retries: 1
  temperature: 0
  output_schema: "pairwise_pref_v1"
  dimensions: ["overall_preference", "format_adherence"]
  score_sampling_rate: 0.25

Acceptance criteria
- [x] eval-harness exposes a JudgeScorer module with pairwise + rubric modes.
- [x] Scorer returns a strict, validated result schema (no free-form text).
- [x] Includes robust parsing/failure handling:
  - invalid JSON -> mark as judge_error with reason
  - timeout -> judge_timeout
  - refusal -> judge_refusal
- [x] Provides a configuration spec (documented) that Shadow Runner can reference; includes template_id, mode, judge_model, safety knobs.
- [x] Emitted result payload conforms to shadow_eval metric/event schema requirements (dims + tag allowlists).
- [x] Unit tests for prompt construction, parser, and aggregation normalization.
- [x] Integration test (can be mocked judge) that simulates shadow run scoring and produces a telemetry event.
- [x] Security review sign-off on what the judge sees (redacted/truncated inputs) and what is logged by eval-harness.

Implementation notes / guardrails
- Judge must never be on the primary request critical path. All scoring is async.
- Cap cost: enforce max judge tokens and timeouts; allow score_sampling_rate < shadow_sampling_rate.
- Avoid feedback loops: do not feed judge output back into user response.
- Redaction: scorer should accept already-redacted inputs (preferred). If scorer performs any redaction, it must use the shared redaction library/config used by Shadow Runner (PR-48288).

Links
- Confluence guidelines: sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness/shadow-llm-judge-scoring-guidelines.json
- Telemetry schema + tagging: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/shadow-eval-metrics-schema-and-tagging.json
- Related PR (eval-harness): sources/github/eval-harness/pr-911.json

Rollout
- Beta: ship with 1–2 Redwood-managed templates:
  - shadow_v1_general_pairwise
  - shadow_v1_json_format_rubric
- Gatekeeping guidance: recommend using win-rate deltas + confidence intervals, not single-day point estimates; avoid gating on rubric dimensions that show low stability.

Open questions
- Where does scoring run for GA: in Shadow Runner workers vs downstream async job? (Leaning: Shadow Runner calls scorer; keep option to move later.)
- Judge model selection policy: do we allow customer-chosen judge models or only Redwood-managed? (Beta: Redwood-managed only.)
- Statistical smoothing/windowing: do we compute CI in Console/analytics or in scorer? (Prefer analytics/Console.)
